recent_posts.title: What's new in TensorFlow 2.20
recent_posts.summary: TensorFlow 2.20 introduces significant changes including the deprecation of tf.lite in favor of LiteRT for on-device inference, which offers improved NPU and GPU acceleration with a unified interface for Neural Processing Units. The release also adds autotune.min_parallelism to tf.data.Options for faster input pipeline warm-up and makes the tensorflow-io-gcs-filesystem package optional, requiring explicit installation for Google Cloud Storage support.

recent_posts.title: What's new in TensorFlow 2.19
recent_posts.summary: TensorFlow 2.19 has been released, featuring updates to the C++ API in LiteRT, bfloat16 support for tflite casting, and the discontinuation of releasing libtensorflow packages. Future releases regarding the new multi-backend Keras will be available on keras.io, starting with Keras 3.0.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Wake Vision: A High-Quality, Large-Scale Dataset for TinyML Computer Vision Applications
recent_posts.summary: Wake Vision is a new large-scale dataset created to advance research and development in TinyML, which focuses on running machine learning models on low-power devices like microcontrollers. The dataset contains approximately 6 million images, nearly 100 times larger than the previous Visual Wake Words (VWW) dataset. Wake Vision offers high-quality labeled images, beneficial for under-parameterized models, and includes fine-grained benchmarks for real-world applications. The dataset is freely available under a permissive license, aiming to help researchers build better person detection models for ultra-low-power devices.

recent_posts.title: MLSysBook.AI: Principles and Practices of Machine Learning Systems Engineering
recent_posts.summary: Machine learning (ML) systems engineering is crucial for transforming sophisticated models into robust, scalable, and efficient systems. MLSysBook.ai fills the educational gap by providing practical insights and resources on ML infrastructure, optimization, deployment, and maintenance, with examples tied to the TensorFlow ecosystem. An interactive learning assistant, SocratiQ, enhances this resource by offering personalized guidance. Understanding both ML modeling and system engineering is key to creating impactful AI solutions.

recent_posts.title: What's new in TensorFlow 2.18
recent_posts.summary: TensorFlow 2.18 has been released with significant updates, including support for NumPy 2.0, which may affect edge cases in API usage. The transition from TFLite to LiteRT has begun, and developers are encouraged to switch over. TensorFlow builds will now include specific versions of CUDA for more reproducible builds and added performance for Ada-Generation GPUs. Support for older GPU versions like Maxwell has been dropped from precompiled packages.

recent_posts.title: What's new in TensorFlow 2.17
recent_posts.summary: TensorFlow 2.17 includes a CUDA update, improvements for Ada-Generation GPUs, and discontinued support for older CUDA kernels. Future release 2.18 will introduce Numpy 2.0 and drop TensorRT support. Updates on the new multi-backend Keras will be on keras.io.

recent_posts.title: Faster Dynamically Quantized Inference with XNNPack
recent_posts.summary: XNNPack's Fully Connected and Convolution 2D operators now support dynamic range quantization, improving CPU inference performance. Dynamic range quantization allows for more AI powered features on older and lower tier devices. The combination of half precision inference and dynamic range quantization results in the best possible on-device CPU inference performance on devices with hardware support.

recent_posts.title: What's new in TensorFlow 2.16
recent_posts.summary: TensorFlow 2.16 has been released with highlights including Clang as default compiler for building TensorFlow CPU wheels on Windows, Keras 3 as default version, and support for Python 3.12.

recent_posts.title: Graph neural networks in TensorFlow
recent_posts.summary: Graph neural networks, or GNNs, are a powerful technique that leverage the graph's connectivity and input features to make predictions about graphs. TF-GNN is a production-tested library for building GNNs at large scale. It supports both modeling and training in TensorFlow and provides tooling for subgraph sampling. GNNs can be trained in an unsupervised way to compute a continuous representation or embedding of the graph structure.

recent_posts.title: TensorFlow 2.15 update: hot-fix for Linux installation issue
recent_posts.summary: A hot-fix has been released for an installation issue affecting TensorFlow 2.15, which requested tensorrt-related packages that were not found. The hot-fix removes these dependencies and allows for the intended installation of TensorFlow 2.15.
